This was the third Professional season in the history of the country. [[Al Wahda FC|Al Wahda]] were defending champions from the [[2009–10 UAE Pro League|2009–10 campaign]]. [[Ajman Club|Ajman]] and [[Emirates Club|Emirates]] were relegated from [[2009–10 UAE Pro League|the previous season]]. [[Dubai CSC|Dubai]] and [[Kalba FC|Ittihad Kalba]] were promoted from the [[UAE First Division League|UAE First Division 1 Group A]]. The campaign began on 26 August 2010 and ended on 9 June 2011.{{cite web|title=match schedule for upcoming ufl season unveiled|url=http://live.proleague.ae/en/news/match-schedule-for-upcoming-ufl-season-unveiled.html|publisher=ProLeague.ae|date=22 July 2010|access-date=5 May 2011}} After being runner-up for three consecutive seasons, [[Al Jazira Club|Al Jazira]] secured their 1st Pro League title after beating [[Al Wasl F.C.|Al Wasl]] 4–0 on 16 May 2011,{{cite web|title=Al Jazira crown themselves champions with a 4–0 win over Al Wasl|url=http://ufl.ae/en/news/al-wasl-vs-al-jazira.html|publisher=[[UAE Football League|UFL]]|date=16 May 2011|access-date=17 May 2011|archive-date=26 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220626225755/http://ufl.ae/en/news/al-wasl-vs-al-jazira.html|url-status=dead}} becoming the third club to achieve the [[Double (association football)|double]] in country's history after [[Al-Nasr SC (Dubai)|Al Nasr]] in 1986 and [[Al Wasl F.C.|Al Wasl]] in 2007.{{cite web|title=Al Jazira at a distance of 3 points to achieve the Double and go down in history|url=http://international.daralhayat.com/internationalarticle/266702|publisher=Dar Al Hayat|date=15 May 2011|access-date=17 May 2011|language=ar|archive-date=17 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317050128/http://international.daralhayat.com/internationalarticle/266702|url-status=usurped}} ==Teams== [[Ajman Club|Ajman]] and [[Emirates Club|Emirates]] were relegated to the second-level league after finishing in the bottom two in the [[2009–10 UAE Pro League|2009–10 season]].
